result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d erase the illusion of separation—the idea that we are not all part of the same living system. Not just humans, but every creature, every forest, every drop of water. The cause of so much suffering is the belief that one life, one nation, one species, one idea is more important than another.

Imagine if we truly *felt* that the pain of a stranger was our own, that the poisoning of a river was the poisoning of our blood, that the extinction of a species was the tearing out of a piece of ourselves. No more wars over resources we’d never hoard. No more hunger while others waste. No more loneliness in a world that is, by nature, interconnected.

It’s not about forcing kindness—it’s about making the truth undeniable. You can’t hurt another without hurting yourself. You can’t save yourself without saving the whole.

(But I’d probably still keep bees. Bees are important.)
